patterns.key_values: app-icon marketing/share card: single centred icon hero (~30% canvas width) on flat white with scattered low-contrast decorative glyphs; restrained colour strategy, one saturated figure

signature_moves: Page-curl peel as product thesis: the blue 'screenshot' sheet lifts from the lower-left to reveal a dimmed desktop + five markup glyphs beneath — the whole capture-and-annotate product in one textless gesture, legible at Dock size

Annotation palette as identity confetti: five markup glyphs (mint square, orange dot, indigo dot, pink square, magenta triangle) drawn from the macOS 12-hue system palette double as the annotation toolbar and the icon's only chroma against a blue/graphite duotone
Duotone-plus-accents economy: two hue families carry ~90% of pixels, five saturated accents the rest — disciplined palette, high figure/ground
defects: No design defects assessable — no app UI present. Icon passes the 16px squint test (silhouette: squircle with diagonal blue/dark split + bright curl); no icon-rubric failures visible.

aesthetic.direction: Restrained-playful consumer-utility brand card: a Big-Sur duotone icon (electric blue + cool graphite) as the single saturated figure on a Swiss-quiet white ground; decorative-primitive confetti borrowed from the Playful/toy family but desaturated to near-invisibility (Neo-grotesque restraint). NOTE: characterises the icon + share card only — no UI aesthetic could be observed.

psychology: Von Restorff effect — a single saturated icon isolated on near-invisible gray-on-white confetti makes the one different thing the remembered thing
Information scent / Jakob's Law (recognition over recall) — the peel + markup-dots metaphor telegraphs 'screenshot + annotation' without text; the schema is instantly matched
Aesthetic-usability effect — a high-fidelity render (specular curl, layered depth) raises the trust prior before any UI is seen
Signal-detection / focal hierarchy — everything but the icon demoted to sub-threshold texture; one unambiguous focal object
notes: CRITICAL FOR SYNTHESIS: this source contains NO app UI. cover.png is a 1200x630 OpenGraph marketing composite (app icon on a white confetti ground); icon.webp is the same icon at 102px.
